extracted.intended_audience: public companies (registrants), GHG attestation providers (auditors and non-accounting verifiers), corporate legal/compliance teams, and investors
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts standards and criteria in the SEC's discussion of assurance and attestation for required climate-related (GHG) disclosures, including who must obtain assurance, what level, attestation provider qualifications, and related procedural requirements. Focused on implementing and complying with Item 1505/1506 assurance rules for registrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase-in timing for assurance (limited → reasonable)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules contemplate a phase-in from limited assurance to reasonable assurance for required Scope 1 and Scope 2 GHG emissions disclosures; commenters recommend varied timelines (e.g., phasing in attestation for largest companies first, multi-year transitions, deferral of attestation requirements for additional years, or acceleration to require limited/reasonable assurance earlier).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters recommended many alternatives (examples: phase-in for public companies over $25B first; extend limited→reasonable period beyond two years; 3–5 year delays for some filers; accelerate to require limited assurance in year 1 and reasonable in year 2). The Commission discusses compliance dates separately (see section II.O.3) and considers supply/capacity to provide assurance when setting phase-in periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'limited assurance' and 'reasonable assurance'
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the Commission should define 'limited assurance' and 'reasonable assurance' and how to do so (e.g., by reference to AICPA and IAASB standards or with Commission-specific definitions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters were split: some asked the Commission to define the terms or describe minimum procedures to reduce ambiguity; others said definitions are not needed because terms are generally understood or exist in AICPA/IAASB standards. Several commenters recommended defining these terms by reference to AICPA and IAASB standards to avoid confusion with other attestation engagements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation provider eligibility and professional requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Attestation providers should comply with a professional framework encompassing competence, independence and a system of quality management; debate over whether eligible providers should be limited to PCAOB-registered audit firms or include non-accounting firms with subject-matter expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many commenters urged competence/independence/quality management systems; some supported allowing engineering/consulting firms (to expand supply and reduce costs) so long as they meet quality standards; others (Better Markets, Mazars, NASBA, RSM) recommended limiting to PCAOB-regulated entities for investor protection and inspection oversight. If non-CPAs are permitted, commenters recommended developing regulations to build the relevant infrastructure (independence requirements, quality management, peer review/inspection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter expertise and experience requirements for attestation providers
rubrics_metrics.description: Attestation providers should have appropriate technical knowledge and competencies in STEM fields related to the sources and sinks of GHG emissions and removals being quantified; 'experience' should be clarified so it ensures proper technical competency rather than rigid years-of-service requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some commenters recommended specifying years of experience; others warned that prescriptive years may limit new businesses despite having qualified personnel. Commenters asked the Commission to provide guidance (similar to S-K 1300's 'qualified person') to ensure consistency and comparability of GHG attestations across registrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter appropriateness as a precondition for assurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Under commonly used attestation standards, the subject matter (e.g., Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions) of the engagement must be appropriate as a precondition for providing assurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the subject matter is appropriate for a limited assurance engagement, it is also appropriate for a reasonable assurance engagement. Attestation standards cited include AICPA SSAE No. 18 and IAASB ISAE 3000 (Revised).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation provider evaluation criteria for registrant disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: A GHG emissions attestation provider is required to include in its evaluation relevant contextual information and evaluate the registrant's compliance with Item 1505(a) presentation requirements and Item 1505(b) disclosure requirements (methodology, organizational boundary, operational boundary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The attestation provider must ensure the registrant's disclosures satisfy presentation and disclosure requirements (for example, disaggregation of constituent gases if individually material). See also Proposing Release, section II.H.1 and cross-references to 17 CFR 229.1506(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope coverage required/voluntary (Scope 1/2 required; Scope 3 voluntary)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules require assurance for Scope 1 and/or Scope 2 emissions pursuant to Item 1506(a); Scope 3 GHG emissions disclosures are not required but may be provided voluntarily by registrants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an LAF is required to obtain reasonable assurance over Scope 1/2 and the attestation provider follows AICPA standards, the LAF could voluntarily obtain limited assurance for voluntary Scope 3 disclosures using the AICPA's attestation standard for limited assurance. Some commenters recommended phased-in treatment or limited assurance for material Scope 3 sources over multi-year timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation engagement period definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'attestation and professional engagement period' means the period covered by the attestation report and the period of the engagement; the professional engagement period begins when the GHG attestation service provider either signs an initial engagement letter (or other agreement) or begins attest procedures, whichever is earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed Item 1505(b)(2)(iv) defined the term; this clarifies when engagement responsibilities commence for purposes of inspection/qualifications/experience and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes of limited versus reasonable assurance
rubrics_metrics.description: A limited assurance engagement results in a conclusion that no material modification is needed; a reasonable assurance engagement results in an opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinction is consistent with attestation frameworks (see supra notes referencing AICPA standards). Commenters argued about which level (limited vs reasonable) is appropriate for investor needs given costs and supply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and reference to established attestation/sustainability assurance standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission and commenters reference established attestation standards (AICPA SSAE No. 18; IAASB ISAE 3000 (Revised)) and international initiatives (IAASB proposed ISSA 5000) as the appropriate frameworks for limited and reasonable assurance engagements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several commenters urged the Commission to define limited/reasonable assurance by reference to those standards rather than creating alternative definitions. The IAASB exposure draft and international/regional regulatory developments (EU CSRD/Directive 2022/2464, California SB-253) were cited as relevant contextual standards and trends toward limited then reasonable assurance transitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum procedures for limited assurance (requested by some commenters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some commenters requested that the Commission describe some minimum procedures that the auditor would be expected to utilize in performing a limited assurance engagement to establish a process more rigorous than current practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests included describing minimum procedures to avoid conflation with informal verification practices and to ensure limited assurance provides meaningful investor protection comparable across registrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory oversight, inspections, and monitoring of attestation providers
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters debated whether eligible providers should be PCAOB-registered (so subject to PCAOB inspection) or whether non-auditor providers may be allowed subject to enhanced SEC monitoring and development of outside inspection/oversight frameworks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments for PCAOB-only providers focused on investor protection and inspectability; arguments for permitting non-accounting firms emphasized expanding the supply of providers and competition. If non-PCAOB providers are allowed, commenters recommended building intellectual infrastructure (independence requirements, quality management systems, peer review/inspections) and enhanced SEC enforcement or monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment and disclosure of fees for GHG attestation engagements
rubrics_metrics.description: If the independent accountant who audits the registrant's consolidated financial statements is also engaged to perform the GHG emissions attestation for the same filing, the fees associated with the GHG emissions attestation engagement would be considered 'Audit-Related Fees' for purposes of proxy/filing fee disclosure (Item 9(e) of 17 CFR 240.14a-101, Item 14 of Form 10-K, Item 16C of Form 20-F, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies how registrants should categorize and disclose attestation-related fees in existing filings and proxy disclosures.
